description: Three cast bars, stamped and stacked. Somebody smelted these, and somebody else never delivered them.
lore: [[characters/2f7f1de9|Halvard]] will weigh them, quote you low, and not move. He does not doubt the metal. It is that [[lore/the_gold_agreement|gold]] is the one substance everybody out of every century remembers identically, and silver is not on that list. Silver arrives arguing. His buyers came out of lives a thousand years apart and every one of them knows exactly what silver is worth, and no two of the numbers agree, and a pedlar who prices in coin and keeps walking can afford one argument a day at the outside.

So a hundred and eighty gold in bars is a fortune that has to be re-agreed at every counter on the road, which is what makes the stamp worth reading. It is a house mark, not a man's name, and the house is not anywhere now. Somebody at the far end waited on a delivery that never came, and it is worth being exact about why: the bars were not lost. They are right here, three of them, stacked as they were poured. It was the road that went.
gm_notes: Establishes the negative space around gold: everything that is not gold has to be re-priced by whoever is at the counter, which is why Halvard's book is in coin. Also a Drift hook — cargo intact, route gone.
